question: Light travels in a:
solution:
The correct answer is __**straight line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Light travels in a straight line in a uniform medium.
 
• This principle is known as the rectilinear propagation of light.
 
• This behavior can be observed in phenomena such as shadows and the way light travels through optical fibers.
 
• Deviation from a straight path occurs due to refraction, reflection, or diffraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction**

 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with different densities.
 
• This change in speed causes the light to change direction.
 
• Common examples include the bending of light when it passes through water or glass.
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it hits a surface.
 
• The angle at which the light hits the surface is equal to the angle at which it reflects off.
 
• Mirrors are a common example where reflection is observed.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**
 
 
• Diffraction is the slight bending of light as it passes around the edge of an object.
 
• This phenomenon is more noticeable with waves of larger wavelengths.
 
• Diffraction can cause light to spread out and create patterns when it passes through small openings or around obstacles.
 
 
 
• **Rectilinear Propagation**
 
 
• Rectilinear propagation states that light travels in straight lines in a homogeneous medium.
 
• This principle is fundamental in understanding the behavior of light and designing optical instruments.
 
• It is the basis for phenomena such as the formation of shadows and the operation of devices like lasers and telescopes.
